item.text: {"schema":"voice-draft-source/3","kind":"draft","ledger":[{"id":"c1","basis":"request-supported","claim":"The listed options on a choice screen are selected by someone with gatekeeper power.","request_basis":"who selects the listed options"},{"id":"c2","basis":"request-supported","claim":"Defaults shape user behaviour.","request_basis":"how defaults shape behaviour"},{"id":"c3","basis":"request-supported","claim":"Nominal choice can preserve gatekeeper power.","request_basis":"why nominal choice can preserve gatekeeper power"},{"id":"c4","basis":"request-supported","claim":"A meaningful remedy would change the structure of the choice.","request_basis":"what a meaningful remedy would change"}],"paragraphs":[{"sentences":[{"text":"Choice screens are not market choice.","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]},{"text":"They can present a neat list of options while leaving the important decision somewhere else: with the person who decided which options appear, which one appears first, and which one is already selected.","basis":"request-supported","claim_ids":["c1"]},{"text":"That isn't a market with many sellers meeting on equal terms.","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]},{"text":"It's a gate with a menu attached.","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]}]},{"sentences":[{"text":"The first question is simple: who selects the list?","basis":"request-supported","claim_ids":["c1"]},{"text":"A choice screen doesn't emerge from nowhere.","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]},{"text":"Someone defines the available categories, removes alternatives that are inconvenient to support, and decides what counts as a reasonable option in the first place.","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]},{"text":"That selection is power before anyone clicks anything.","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]}]},{"sentences":[{"text":"For software developers, this matters because the interface can make an upstream decision look like a downstream preference.","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]},{"text":"If the system offers three tools, the user appears to be choosing among three tools—but only within the boundary somebody else drew.","basis":"request-supported","claim_ids":["c1","c3"]},{"text":"The missing option doesn't need to be rejected by the user; it only needs to be absent.","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]},{"text":"And absence is difficult to measure when the screen reports a successful selection.","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]}]},{"sentences":[{"text":"Defaults deepen the problem.","basis":"request-supported","claim_ids":["c2"]},{"text":"The preselected option has already won a small argument before the user begins one.","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]},{"text":"It saves a click, supplies a recommendation, and gives hesitation a direction—especially when the alternatives are less visible or require more explanation.","basis":"request-supported","claim_ids":["c2"]},{"text":"The user may still be able to change it, but the system has shaped the path of least resistance.","basis":"request-supported","claim_ids":["c2"]}]},{"sentences":[{"text":"Is that really choice?","basis":"request-supported","claim_ids":["c2","c3"]},{"text":"Sometimes it is, but the existence of an escape hatch does not settle the question.","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]},{"text":"A person can technically refuse a default and still be guided by it.","basis":"request-supported","claim_ids":["c2"]},{"text":"Choice is not only the final click; it is also the arrangement that makes one click feel ordinary and another feel like work.","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]}]},{"sentences":[{"text":"This is how nominal choice preserves gatekeeper power.","basis":"request-supported","claim_ids":["c3"]},{"text":"The gatekeeper can say that users are free to choose, while retaining control over the boundaries, labels, order, and defaults that give the choice its meaning.","basis":"request-supported","claim_ids":["c1","c2","c3"]},{"text":"The interface becomes a kind of card catalog whose librarian decides which books deserve a shelf—and then places one book open on the desk.","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]},{"text":"The catalog looks plural; the collection is still curated.","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]}]},{"sentences":[{"text":"That distinction matters more than the comforting language of flexibility.","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]},{"text":"A developer can build a screen that satisfies the formal requirement to offer options while making the practical result nearly inevitable.","basis":"request-supported","claim_ids":["c3"]},{"text":"The code can be clean, the labels can be accurate, and the user can still receive a managed decision rather than a meaningful one.","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]},{"text":"Technical neutrality cannot be created by placing a few buttons on the page.","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]}]},{"sentences":[{"text":"A meaningful remedy would change who controls the choice, not merely how many choices are displayed.","basis":"request-supported","claim_ids":["c4","c1"]},{"text":"It would require the listed options to reflect a genuinely broader field, with no important alternative hidden by the screen's architecture.","basis":"request-supported","claim_ids":["c4"]},{"text":"It would also treat defaults as substantive decisions rather than harmless interface decoration.","basis":"request-supported","claim_ids":["c2","c4"]},{"text":"If a default changes behaviour, then choosing that default is an exercise of power—and it should be examined as such.","basis":"request-supported","claim_ids":["c2","c3"]}]},{"sentences":[{"text":"That does not mean every screen must become unusable, or that every option deserves equal prominence regardless of context.","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]},{"text":"It means the convenience of the interface cannot be purchased by concealing the decision that produced it.","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]},{"text":"A remedy could preserve useful guidance while making the basis for that guidance visible, the alternatives reachable, and the cost of declining the recommendation reasonable.","basis":"request-supported","claim_ids":["c4"]},{"text":"The point is not to eliminate design; it is to stop design from impersonating consent.","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]}]},{"sentences":[{"text":"Developers should therefore ask a harder question than whether a choice screen contains multiple buttons.","basis":"normative","claim_ids":[]},{"text":"Who chose these options?","basis":"request-supported","claim_ids":["c1"]},{"text":"Which option does the system quietly favour, and what behaviour follows from that favouring?","basis":"request-supported","claim_ids":["c2"]},{"text":"If the answer is that the gatekeeper still controls the menu and the path, then the screen has changed the appearance of power, not its location.","basis":"request-supported","claim_ids":["c2","c3"]},{"text":"Build the remedy around that reality.","basis":"normative","claim_ids":[]}]},{"sentences":[{"text":"A market choice gives people room to decide among meaningful alternatives.","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]},{"text":"A choice screen can give them only the room its designer has left open.","basis":"request-supported","claim_ids":["c1","c3"]},{"text":"The difference is not cosmetic.","basis":"reasoning","claim_ids":[]},{"text":"It is the difference between choosing inside a system and having a say over the system that does the choosing.","basis":"request-supported","claim_ids":["c4"]}]}],"omitted":[{"habit":"opponents-allies-sources / o11: named allies and hyperlinked sources","why":"The request supplies no sources, allies, or co-signatories to name or link."}],"refused":""}
